title: What Software Handles Broker Compliance Tasks? A Guide for Loan Brokers and ISOs
summary: No single tool covers broker compliance. Loan brokers pair a lending platform with a registration tracker; broker-dealers add supervision tools.
body_markdown:
Compliance work for many brokers still lives in spreadsheets, inboxes, and shared drives. That setup makes it easy to miss a deadline or lose a signed form. This guide explains what software handles broker compliance tasks, which rules create those tasks, and how to pick tools that fit your firm.


### What Software Handles Broker Compliance Tasks?


No single tool handles every broker compliance task, so most firms combine a few types of compliance software. Loan brokers usually pair a lending platform for documents, data, and disclosures with a tracker for state registrations. Broker-dealers add supervision, surveillance, and archiving tools built for securities rules.


Compliance software is any tool that helps a firm follow the laws and rules for its business. Software can run the steps, but your firm stays responsible for getting them right. Rules change often, so review your setup with a lawyer who knows your states and products.


Here are the main types of compliance tools brokers use:


- **Lending or broker platforms:** Collect documents, business identity data, signed disclosures, and borrower messages in one deal file.
- **Registration and licensing trackers:** Track state registration dates, renewal deadlines, and filing records for each state where you work.
- **Compliance management software:** Assign tasks, store policies, and log reviews across a team. General GRC (governance, risk, and compliance) tools fit here.
- **Broker-dealer supervision and archiving tools:** Review trades and messages, flag issues, and keep records in the format securities rules expect.


Lendflow fits in the first group.[Lendflow's broker platform](https://www.lendflow.com/lendflow-for-brokers) supports multi-lender submission, deal tracking, document collection, AI communications, and commission tracking in one workflow. Lendflow is not a compliance or GRC product, so pair it with the tools and legal advice your obligations require.


### Which Kind of Broker Are You? Compliance Differs by Type


The word "broker" covers very different businesses, and each type answers to different rules. A commercial loan broker or ISO (independent sales organization) connects businesses with lenders and funders. A broker-dealer trades securities, such as stocks and bonds, under FINRA (Financial Industry Regulatory Authority) and SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission) rules.


Embedded-finance teams often sit between these two groups. A software company that offers funding inside its product may refer customers to lenders. That role can raise the same disclosure and registration questions a loan broker faces.


If you place business loans or merchant cash advances (MCAs), broker dealer compliance software is likely the wrong fit for your work. The table below shows how the regulatory compliance software needs of each type differ.


Commercial loan broker or ISO Broker-dealer


Main regulators State agencies, such as the Texas OCCC, California DFPI, and New York DFS FINRA and the SEC


Key rules State commercial financing disclosure and registration laws FINRA Rule 3110 supervision, Reg BI, and anti-money laundering rules


Core tasks Deliver disclosures, track registrations, collect KYB data for lenders, and keep deal records Supervise staff, review trades and messages, document recommendations, and archive records


Typical software A lending or broker platform plus a registration tracker Supervision, surveillance, and archiving tools


#### Broker-Dealer Rules That Shape Software Needs


Broker-dealers face two well-known rule sets that shape their software needs. Under[FINRA Rule 3110 supervision](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/notices/14-10) , a firm needs a supervisory system "reasonably designed to achieve compliance" with securities laws and FINRA rules. Supervision tools support that system by logging reviews, approvals, and escalations.


Regulation Best Interest, or Reg BI, governs how broker-dealers recommend securities to retail customers. The[SEC's Reg BI bulletin](https://www.sec.gov/about/divisions-offices/division-trading-markets/broker-dealers/staff-bulletin-standards-conduct-broker-dealers-investment-advisers-conflicts-interest) lists four component obligations: Disclosure, Care, Conflict of Interest, and Compliance. Reg BI covers securities advice, so it does not shape commercial lending workflows.


### The Compliance Tasks Commercial Loan Brokers Handle


For loan brokers and ISOs, state laws drive most compliance work. Each state sets its own rules for disclosures, registration, and records, so your task list depends on where your clients do business.


Below are five task groups, along with the software job each one creates. Use them to build your own compliance tracking list.


#### Deliver State Commercial Financing Disclosures


A commercial financing disclosure is a standard form that shows a business the cost and terms of an offer before it signs. Buchalter's summary of the[California commercial disclosure regulations](https://www.buchalter.com/insights/california-dfpi-publishes-final-commercial-loan-disclosure-regulations/) says the rules took effect December 9, 2022, for offers of $500,000 or less.


New York's rules reach larger deals. Buchalter reports that[New York's disclosure law](https://www.buchalter.com/insights/ny-dfs-publishes-final-regulation-implementing-article-8-new-york-states-commercial-finance-disclosure-law/) required compliance from August 1, 2023, for financing of up to $2,500,000. When a broker is involved, the provider must also tell the business how the broker is paid and who pays them.


The software job is to generate the right form, deliver it, capture the e-signature, and store the signed copy. An e-signature is a signature captured online. A time-stamped copy shows when the client received and signed the form.


Because each state sets its own thresholds, your tool should choose the form based on the client's location and the offer amount. A $750,000 offer, for example, is above California's $500,000 limit but within New York's $2,500,000 limit.


#### Stay Ahead of Broker Registration and Renewals


Some states now require commercial finance brokers to register before doing business. The[Texas HB 700 enrolled text](https://capitol.texas.gov/tlodocs/89R/billtext/html/HB00700F.HTM) says existing sales-based financing brokers and providers must register by December 31, 2026. Each violation can bring a $10,000 civil penalty.


Sales-based financing is funding repaid from a share of a business's future sales, such as an MCA. The Texas Office of Consumer Credit Commissioner (OCCC) enforces the law, and registrations must be renewed by January 31 each year. As of November 2026, that first deadline is only weeks away.


The same bill also requires providers to give a disclosure with specific sales-based financing offers under $1 million. That means Texas MCA deals can create both a registration task and a disclosure task.


The software job here is deadline tracking. A registration calendar should list each state, filing date, renewal date, and task owner. If you work mostly with MCA deals, our guide to[ISO software for MCA brokers](https://www.lendflow.com/post/iso-software-for-merchant-cash-advance-features-compliance-and-how-to-choose) covers tools for that workflow.


#### Collect KYB and Beneficial Ownership Data


KYB, short for Know Your Business, is the process of confirming a business is real and identifying who owns or controls it. Lenders and their bank partners often need this data before they fund a deal, and brokers often collect it for them.


FinCEN, the Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, sets the customer due diligence (CDD) rule for banks, broker-dealers, and certain other institutions. Loan brokers are not on that list. Even so, your lender partners may ask you to collect the same data under your contracts, so read your partner agreements closely.


Under the rule, beneficial owners include anyone who owns 25% or more of a company, plus one person who controls it. That is why[FinCEN's CDD rule FAQs](https://www.fincen.gov/resources/statutes-and-regulations/cdd-rule-faqs) say a legal entity has between one and five beneficial owners. Our[KYB verification process](https://www.lendflow.com/post/kyb-verification) guide walks through how to gather this data in a consistent format.


#### Keep Audit-Ready Records and Audit Trails


An audit trail is a time-stamped record of who did what on a deal, and when. If a lender partner or regulator asks questions, you need the documents, offers, disclosures, and messages for that deal in one place.


Scattered files make that hard, and compliance audit software only works with the records you feed it.[AI document analysis](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/doc-analyzer) identifies, classifies, and extracts data from files like bank statements and tax returns, so records stay consistent. Lendflow's[end-to-end borrower communications](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/end-to-end-communications) tools keep text messages, calls, and deal notes connected to the same workflow.


A complete deal file usually holds the application, bank statements, KYB data, each offer, the signed disclosure, and client messages. Keeping these items together lets you answer a lender partner's questions without searching several systems.


#### Prepare for Data Collection Rules on the Horizon


Section 1071 of the Dodd-Frank Act requires covered financial institutions to collect and report data on small business credit applications. As of November 2026, the[CFPB small business lending rule](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/compliance/compliance-resources/small-business-lending-resources/small-business-lending-collection-and-reporting-requirements/) page says the CFPB extended the compliance date to January 1, 2028.


The CFPB, or Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, says it will update its guidance materials later. The[CFPB's 2026 final rule](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-policy/final-rules/small-business-lending-under-the-equal-credit-opportunity-act-regulation-b-2026/) lists an effective date of June 30, 2026. Coverage depends on your role in each deal, so ask counsel whether the rule reaches your firm before you build a new data process.


### Features to Look for in Broker Compliance Software


Once you know your tasks, you can judge compliance management software by how well it handles each one.


Compliance monitoring software watches for missed steps, such as an unsigned disclosure, and alerts the task owner. Compliance tracking software records what was done and when. Look for these features when you compare broker compliance software and compliance monitoring tools:


- **Disclosure generation:** Builds state-specific disclosure forms from deal data so the terms match the offer.
- **E-signature capture:** Records each signed form with a time stamp and stores it with the deal.
- **Registration calendar:** Tracks state filings, renewal dates, and owners, with reminders before each deadline.
- **KYB and data verification:** Collects business identity and ownership data and checks it against outside sources.
- **Document validation:** Classifies uploaded files and flags missing or mismatched information.
- **Logged communications:** Saves borrower messages, calls, and notes in the deal record.
- **Audit-ready exports:** Pulls a full deal file, with dates, into one report for a lender or regulator.
- **Lender integrations and APIs:** Connects to lender partners so data moves without retyping. An API (application programming interface) lets two systems share data automatically.


Data checks deserve extra attention because one wrong entry flows into every later step. Before you choose a tool, learn how to[verify borrower data step by step](https://www.lendflow.com/post/how-do-brokers-verify-borrower-data-a-step-by-step-guide) .


### How to Choose the Right Compliance Tools


**80% smaller teams:** According to Lendflow, its embedded finance customers operate with 80% smaller teams while converting similar funding volumes.


Lean teams like these need compliance tools that fit the daily workflow instead of adding manual steps.


Use these five steps to choose compliance tracking software and related tools:


1. **Map your obligations:** List every state and product you work with, then note the disclosure, registration, and data rules for each.
2. **List your tasks:** Turn each rule into a task, such as delivering a New York disclosure or renewing a Texas registration.
3. **Check integrations:** Confirm the tool connects to your lender partners, CRM (customer relationship management system), and document storage.
4. **Test with a real deal file:** Run one recent deal through the tool and check whether you can export a complete record.
5. **Assign owners:** Give every task a named person who reviews the output and signs off.


Watch for these common mistakes when you set up your tools:


- **Relying on spreadsheets for deadlines:** One bad edit can hide a renewal date. Calendar reminders with named owners are easier to check.
- **Storing disclosures outside the deal file:** Separate folders make it hard to show which form went with which offer.
- **Buying broker-dealer tools for lending work:** Securities supervision features rarely match state disclosure and registration tasks.
- **Skipping partner contract reviews:** Lender agreements may add KYB or record duties that no state law lists.
- **Treating software output as final:** A person should check each form before it goes to a client.


Software can only follow the setup you give it, so review your task map with counsel at least once a year. ### Frequently Asked Questions About Broker Compliance Software


These short answers cover common questions about compliance software for brokers. Each answer ties back to the rules explained above.


#### What Is Regulatory Compliance Software?


Regulatory compliance software is any tool that helps a firm track, complete, and record the tasks that laws and rules require. It includes general GRC platforms, registration trackers, and lending platforms that organize deal records.


#### Can One Platform Cover Every Broker Compliance Task?


Usually not, because disclosure, registration, data, and record tasks often live in different systems. A common setup pairs a lending platform with a registration tracker, plus regular review by counsel.


#### How Is Broker-Dealer Compliance Software Different From Loan Broker Tools?


Broker-dealer compliance software focuses on FINRA and SEC needs, such as supervision, trade surveillance, and message archiving. Loan broker tools focus on state disclosures, registrations, KYB data, and deal records.


#### Do Texas Loan Brokers Need to Register?


Under HB 700, brokers and providers of commercial sales-based financing already operating in Texas must register with the OCCC by December 31, 2026. Brokers of other loan types should confirm with counsel whether the law reaches them.


#### Does Section 1071 Apply Now?


Not yet, because as of November 2026 the CFPB's compliance date is January 1, 2028. Whether it will cover your firm depends on your role in each deal, so check with counsel.
